## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khajjopanakajātaka* (Ja 364) is a short text in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon, titled "The Firefly". In the standard Jātaka commentary, the entry under this title is abbreviated: it opens with the lemma *Ko nu santamhi pajjote ti* and notes that the narrative and full exposition of the "Question about a Firefly" (*Khajjopanakapañho*) will be set forth in detail in the *Mahāummagga* [Fausböll 1883].

The full verse and narrative context appear later in the *Mahāummagga-jātaka* in the sixth volume of the Jātaka collection, where a deity recites this "Question about a Firefly" from the Pañcanipāta (*imam Pañcanipāte Khajjopanakapañham udāhari*), rebuking the king with the parable of a foolish person who in the dark mistakes a firefly (*khajjota*) for a flame (*jātaveda*) and vainly attempts to light grass and dung with it [Fausböll 1896].
